"Double The Money" has gone three months without a top prize claim, and tickets kept selling. Only a fixed number of tickets are printed. About half of the tickets are sold, and every remaining $100,000 prize is still unclaimed. That leaves the same top prizes among fewer tickets.

The table below shows the full count for "Double The Money", with every prize level included.
2415.headline: No top prize claimed lately

2416.body:
Of all the tickets printed for "Loaded with $2,000s", about a third are still unsold. The game is well into its run, with 1,128 of 3,372 top prizes unclaimed. In every scratcher, either the tickets or the prizes run out first. The rest of this page shows the details.

Every line of Loaded with $2,000s's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
2416.headline: Tickets sold so far

2419.body:
"Bronze 7s" has one of four top prizes left and is in the second half of its run. About three-quarters of the tickets are already sold. As a game goes on, the same prizes are spread across fewer tickets. Right now, neither the tickets nor the top prizes are running out faster than the other.

If "Bronze 7s" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
2419.headline: Early stage or late

2420.body:
"Silver 7s" is in the middle of its run, with about half of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, a larger share of the top prizes is left than of the tickets, which is a good sign.

Today's free summary of "Silver 7s" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
2420.headline: Tickets sold so far

2421.body:
"Gold 7s" has 184,611 prizes of $10 still unclaimed, which is its most common win. Just below the top prize is the $7,000 prize, with eight left. The full count for every prize level is listed below.

Tomorrow's count on "Gold 7s" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
2421.headline: The prize table, line by line

2422.body:
"Platinum 7s" offers a top prize of $2 million and eleven prize levels in all. The prize money leans about evenly between small prizes and large ones. Games shaped like this offer both kinds of prizes without favoring either. This design never changes, while every other number on this page does.

The numbers for "Platinum 7s" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
2422.headline: How this game pays out

2426.body:
The most common win left on "HAUNTED HUNDREDS" is $2. The second biggest prize left is $50, and 515 of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

If you play "HAUNTED HUNDREDS" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
2426.headline: The prize table, line by line

2427.body:
"HOLIDAY TRIPLER" has 384,282 prizes of $1 still unclaimed, which is its most common win. Just below the top prize is the $100 prize, with 94 left. The full count for every prize level is listed below.

The table below shows the full count for "HOLIDAY TRIPLER", with every prize level included.
2427.headline: Prize table details

2428.body:
"PEPPERMINT PAYOUT" is early in its run, with about three-quarters of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, the top prizes are being claimed more slowly than the tickets are selling, which is a good sign.

If "PEPPERMINT PAYOUT" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
2428.headline: Where this game is in its run

2429.body:
"MERRY MONEY TREE" has fewer top prizes left. The count changed when one top prize of $125,000 was claimed last week. Unsold tickets still hold three of the original four. Check the top prize count first when you compare scratchers.

Everything above about "MERRY MONEY TREE" comes from the Virginia Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
2429.headline: Top prize count went down

2430.body:
"WRAPPED IN RICHES" has had no $500,000 top prize claimed since we started watching it. Everyday prizes keep getting claimed, and fewer tickets are left each day. The number of tickets printed is fixed. Each day without a top prize claim leaves those prizes among fewer tickets.

Tomorrow's count on "WRAPPED IN RICHES" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
2430.headline: No new top prize claims
